To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
firms offshore innovation when they are exposed to high uncertainty about technological change and when they lack the technological capabilities to cope with this uncertainty.
firms with high technological capability are less likely to outsource innovation activities when uncertainty about future technological change is high.

(i) technological dynamism drives firms to offshore innovation, (ii) technological uncertainty about future technological change reduces the probability of offshoring innovation for firms with high internal technological capabilities but not for firms with low capabilities, (iii) this difference in offshoring behavior reflects differing strategic objectives of firms with high and low capabilities, and (iv) firms with high technological capability prefer onshore innovation to keep strong control of their key technological assets.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how firms decide to offshore their innovation activities.
the conditions under which innovation offshoring is more or less likely.
the role of technological capabilities and technological change in the offshoring of innovation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
firms offshoring innovation are those with low technological capabilities and high speed of technological development.
technological uncertainty is not a sufficient condition for innovation offshoring.
firms with low technological dynamism and low technological capability offshore innovation more frequently than other firms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
firms offshore innovation to reduce uncertainty about the future, but the effect depends on the firm’s own technological capability.

firms with high technological capability are more likely to innovate onshore than firms with low technological capability, and that this effect is more pronounced in the presence of high technological uncertainty.
firms offshore innovation to reduce the uncertainty of technological change, but only for firms with weak technological capabilities.
The main takeaway from our work is that
firms with high technological capability are less likely to engage in innovation offshoring when technological uncertainty is high.
firms with high technological capability and technological dynamism are more likely to innovate onshore.
the decision to offshore innovation is not only driven by technological capabilities but also by the technological dynamism of the firm environment.
